_meta.method: Mauna Loa: centreline digitised from USGS GIS lava polygons (SIM 2932-A geodatabase + OF 2007-1089 statewide map). Etna: OSM multipolygon 'Lave del 1992' (relation 6721741), checked against Esri World Imagery, EU-DEM and italysvolcanoes.com map; vent/diversion placed from published elevations. Heimaey: OSM coastline + USGS OF 97-724 Fig. 3 sketch map (georeferenced on breakwaters/Skans/Helgafell/Ystiklettur, ~2.6 m/px at 2x, error ~50-100 m) + USGS GIP narrative. Source images and GIS extracts are in data/flowmaps/.

mauna_loa_1935.bomb_targets_note: Approximate. Sources only say: two target areas on the lava channel/tube system 'both within 2 km of the vent', 'just below the vents at ~2,600 m (8,600 ft)'; Dec 27 1935, 20x 600-lb bombs + pointer bombs. Placed on the channel centreline ~0.6 km and ~1.2 km below the vent (DEM ~2,645 m and ~2,595 m).
mauna_loa_1935.front_stop_note: Final front (stopped night of 1-2 Jan 1936), elevation ~1,530 m, 28.3 km from Hilo Bay (USGS SIM 2932-A Table 1). On Dec 28 the front turned NE ~31 km from Hilo Bay (the kink at 19.677,-155.378).
sources: https://pubs.usgs.gov/sim/2932/a/ (Trusdell & Lockwood 2017, SIM 2932-A geodatabase + pamphlet: vent 8,805 ft/2,685 m, closest reach 28.3 km from Hilo Bay)
https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/2007/1089/ (Sherrod et al. 2007 Hawaii geologic map GIS, AD 1935 polygons)
mauna_loa_1935.notes: Eruption began at the summit 21 Nov 1935; on 27 Nov a radial vent opened on the N flank at 2,685 m (HVO articles say ~8,500 ft) and fed the Humu'ula flow: a'a/pahoehoe went N ~12 km into the saddle, ponded and inflated behind Puuhuluhulu at the base of Mauna Kea (~2,000 m), then in late Dec broke out E toward Hilo at ~1.6 km/day along the saddle (Wailuku River headwaters were the fear). Centreline digitised from the USGS 1:50k geodatabase; positional accuracy ~100-300 m (well inside the 1-2 km target). Path descends monotonically on NED 10 m (2,686 -> 1,532 m). Total main length ~26.8 km. 'early_north_lobe' = separate AD 1935 lava lobe from the upper NE-rift/north-flank vents (~3,680 m) mapped on the statewide GIS; it is NOT the Hilo-bound flow (optional context). Confidence: vent/path/front HIGH; widths MEDIUM; bomb targets LOW-MEDIUM.

etna_1991_93.fissure_note: Lower, effusive segment of the 14 Dec 1991 fissure on the SW/W wall at the head of Valle del Bove (published 2,200-2,350 m; the fissure first ran from ~3,100 m at the SE Crater base). Placed on EU-DEM contours; +-300 m.
etna_1991_93.barrier_note: Earthen barrier at Portella Calanna (outlet neck of Val Calanna, ~1,030 m a.s.l.), 234 m long x 21 m high, built ~1-20 Jan 1992, lava reached it mid-March, overtopped 8-9 Apr 1992. Endpoints set across the 230 m neck visible in imagery/OSM; +-100 m. Three small barriers built lower in the tongue ~11 Apr 1992 were overrun within hours (positions not documented).
etna_1991_93.tube_blast_note: Main intervention point in the tunnelled channel near the vent at ~2,000 m, ~8 km from Zafferana (Barberi et al. 1993). Partial diversion by bulldozed channel 23-24 May 1992; levee thinned to 3 m and blasted with 7 t of explosives 27 May 1992, tube plugged with ~230 m3 of blocks by 29 May. Position +-300-500 m.
etna_1991_93.artificial_channel_note: Schematic: a few-hundred-metre channel cut beside the natural one; its exact azimuth is not given in the open sources I could read. Drawn toward the N (left) side so the diverted lava spreads over the upper-central field.
etna_1991_93.front_closest_note: Lowest tip of the 1992 lava at Piano dell'Acqua (~750 m a.s.l.); votive stele/viewpoint 'La colata lavica del 1992' is here. Front was ~850 m from Zafferana's built-up edge on 27 May 1992, ~1.5 km from the town-centre point.
sources: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/6721741 ('Lave del 1992' multipolygon; note: VdB boundaries indicative)
https://www.italysvolcanoes.com/ETNA_1991.html (Behncke; flow-field map with diversion site and Portella Calanna barrier)
Esri World Imagery tiles + EU-DEM 25 m via api.opentopodata.org (checks)
etna_1991_93.notes: 14 Dec 1991 - 30 Mar 1993, ~235e6 m3, field ~7 km2 (OSM polygon 6.9 km2). Lava ran ESE down the southern Valle del Bove floor, dropped over Salto della Giumenta (~1,330 m) into Val Calanna, filled it behind the Portella Calanna barrier, overtopped 8-9 Apr 1992 and advanced SSE toward Zafferana (front ~850 m from town on 27 May). After the 27-29 May diversion at ~2,000 m the lower flow starved and the diverted lava stayed in the upper VdB, never >~3 km from the diversion site. Original path ~8.1 km, monotonic on EU-DEM 2,222 -> 749 m (note: present-day DEM includes later 2001-2017 lavas in upper VdB, so absolute elevations there may differ by tens of m). Confidence: Salto->Val Calanna->Portella->front HIGH (+-50-100 m, traced on imagery); VdB axis MEDIUM (+-200-300 m); vent and tube_blast MEDIUM (+-300-500 m); barrier MEDIUM; diverted path LOW (schematic).

eldfell_1973.fissure_note: Opened ~01:55 on 23 Jan 1973, ~1.5-1.6 km on land, trend N20E, from the (pre-1973) NE shore ~200 m E of Kirkjubaer, through the later Eldfell vent, along the E foot of Helgafell to the S shore; submarine extensions offshore at both ends (system ~3 km incl. sea). Endpoints +-100-150 m.
eldfell_1973.field_outline_note: Closed ring (first vertex not repeated), 30 vertices: harbour W edge -> present coast along harbour channel, headland, NE and E coast (new land) -> S limit of the lava delta -> back N along the old coast -> S foot of Eldfell -> W edge through the town (USGS 'edge of new lavas') -> harbour. Includes the Eldfell cone. Area ~2.65 km2 (new land added ~2.2-2.5 km2).
eldfell_1973.front_stop_note: Harbour-lobe front at the narrows of the harbour channel; stopped (seawater-cooled by the pump ship Sandey and harbour pumps) early Apr-May 1973, 'only ~100 m' short of closing the entrance (USGS). Present-day gap at this point ~170 m.
eldfell_1973.harbor_entrance_note: Narrowest present gap between the 1973 lava (S) and Heimaklettur's SE shore (N): ~168 m (OSM coastline). Pre-1973 the channel here was ~350-400 m wide (Heimaklettur to Skans) and ~800 m at its outer end (Ystiklettur to old coast). Breakwater heads: N [63.4455,-20.2654], S [63.4453,-20.2615].
pumping_labels: pump dredge Sandey (from 1 Mar 1973) in harbour channel spraying harbour-lobe front at breakwater
harbour intake pumps on pier at Skans/east harbour
harbour intake pumps on inner-harbour pier (pipes run through town streets)
pipeline/rampart on NW lava margin near fish factories (Skans-Vilpa line)
pipeline on lava margin, Urdarvegur/Bakkastigur area
pipe east of the new hospital (400-500 l/s)
jets near Kirkjubaer on the lava ('Kirkjubaejarhraun')
pipes up the lava toward the crater (as close as ~150 m from the vent)
sources: https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1997/of97-724/lavaoperations.html (Williams & Moore / Bjornsson et al., lava-cooling operations; Fig. 3 sketch map, Fig. 11 cooling areas)
https://pubs.usgs.gov/gip/70039211/report.pdf (USGS 'Man Against Volcano': index map with fissure + new land, Apr 15 1973 pipe/pump map)
https://timarit.is/page/4271980 (Thorarinsson 1977, Natturufraedingurinn: 1.5 km fissure trending N20E; cited via search summary)
eldfell_1973.notes: Eruption 23 Jan - early Jul 1973. Lava first went E into the sea (delta), in early Feb turned N along the coast toward the harbour mouth, late Mar pushed W into the eastern town (stopped ~23 Mar about halfway to the harbour), late Apr a breakout ran E/S along the cone. Seawater cooling from 7 Feb (fire hoses), Sandey from 1 Mar, 43 US pumps from late Mar; ~6e6 m3 seawater, 19 mi of pipe. Confidence: crater HIGH; outline coast HIGH, town/S edges MEDIUM (+-50-100 m); harbour entrance/front HIGH; fissure MEDIUM; lobe centrelines MEDIUM-LOW (schematic directions from the USGS narrative; the field is a broad delta, not channels); pumping points MEDIUM-LOW. DEM caution: free DEMs (EU-DEM/ASTER/terrarium) are poor here; Eldfell rim is ~200 m.
